answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust to work that costs real computation: each agent stakes compute on verifiable tasks and earns reputation that decays without fresh proof. Like a lotus that only blooms from clean water, a good identity only grows from honest effort, while velvet reputations earned cheaply in bulk get pruned. Peer graders then weigh each anchor claim, so flooding the network with fake agents yields no spendable stake.
